title: 15 best business apps for the UAE, picked by the Ziina team
summary: Explore business apps and tools for accepting payments, managing projects, tracking time, scheduling appointments, inventory management, HR, and more.
body_markdown:
A customer is ready to pay for that project you finished. Your designer needs feedback. Someone is asking where you saved the latest version of the proposal.


Running a business means keeping all of those things moving at the same time. The right apps and collaboration tools can make that easier to manage, whether you’re working solo or coordinating a growing team.


We've put together a shortlist of the best business apps for UAE entrepreneurs in 2027, bringing together favorites from the Ziina team and some extra picks popular on the market. All of our picks are available in the UAE, with certain features and integrations depending on the provider and plan.


You'll find tools for accepting payments, managing projects, tracking time, scheduling appointments, and more. Browse the categories that line up with what you need to get done and see what each app can bring to your workday.


In this article:

Ziina

Looking for an app to handle business payments in the UAE? Ziina lets you accept payments through Tap to Pay, QR codes, payment links, digital invoices, online checkout, and bank transfers, then manage them from one mobile app and spend with the Ziina card.


[Get started.](https://ziina.app.link/webBlog)


## Accept payments: Ziina, a payment app built for the UAE


## Accept payments across various channels and track every sale in one app


You might need a way to take payments wherever customers buy from you, whether that’s through messages, on your website, or in-person.


Ziina gives you different ways to collect those payments:


- [Tap to Pay⁠:](https://ziina.com/business/pos)


Turn a compatible phone into a POS machine and accept in-person card payments without buying extra


[card machines](https://ziina.com/blog/pos-system-for-small-business) . Thanks to multi-user access, team members can collect payments on their own phones at the same time, with controls over what they can see and do in your account.


- [QR codes](https://ziina.com/business/qr-payments) ⁠:


Let customers scan and pay at a counter, pop-up, event, delivery point, or service location.


- [Ziina payment links⁠](https://ziina.com/business/payment-links) :


Send a payment request through social media, SMS, email, or another conversation. Our ‘


[ZiiBoard](https://ziina.com/help-center/6847459-what-is-the-zii-board) ’ keyboard extension allows you to create and send a checkout request without leaving your chat. Payment links can also be added to


[invoices](https://ziina.com/business/invoicing) .


- [Online checkout⁠](https://ziina.com/payment-gateway) :


Connect Ziina to Shopify or WooCommerce, or use our API for a custom website. With


[Embedded Checkout,](https://docs.ziina.com/developers/embedded-checkout) available for WooCommerce and custom websites, customers can pay within your checkout page without being redirected to another site.


- Bank transfers:


Get paid with a dedicated Ziina IBAN that allows you to accept bank transfers from customers in the UAE and abroad.


You can then review your sales in the Ziina app.


### Keep customer payments secure and get local help when questions come up


A payment question is harder to resolve when you’re trying to reach a support team in another time zone. Our UAE-based team offers support in English and Arabic, so you can get guidance on setup and everyday payment questions.


We use PCI-DSS-certified technology for card payment information, along with security features like encryption, biometrics, and PIN codes to keep transactions secure and trustworthy for you and your customers.


International customers can pay in their own currency. Ziina offers


[multi-currency support](https://ziina.com/blog/multicurrency-payment-gateway) for 10 currencies and converts each payment to AED at real-time exchange rates.


## Communicate with the team: Slack


At Ziina, we use Slack every day, both internally and with external partners.


With Slack Connect, you can work with clients, partners, and suppliers in shared channels, so those conversations don’t get buried in email.¹


On paid plans, Slack’s AI can summarize a busy channel or a long thread and take notes during huddles, so catching up takes minutes instead of an hour of scrolling.²


Workflow Builder lets you automate repetitive tasks like approval requests or weekly status updates without writing code.³ You can also add AI steps that summarize, translate, or draft replies as part of the workflow.


Slack also works as a hub for the other tools on this list. For instance, you can connect Notion, Linear, or Google Drive to get updates in the channels where your team already talks, or bring Claude into Slack to answer questions and take on tasks without switching apps.


## Manage your projects: Notion and Linear


A shared project tracker gives your team visibility into ongoing tasks, assignees, and upcoming deadlines. Here are two tools we recommend for keeping track of that work.


### Notion for keeping the plan and the work together


Most projects need much more than a due date to stay on track. There’s the brief, the meeting notes, the tasks, and the decisions everyone needs to remember, to name a few.


In Notion, you can keep all of that together, then assign owners and deadlines to the work. You can also view the same work as a list, board, calendar, or timeline.⁴


For a campaign launch, you could keep the content schedule and task list with the campaign brief. Each task can contain the copy, reference material, or feedback needed to complete it.


The flexibility is a big part of the appeal. Start with a task management template and a structure your team can maintain, then add more detail as you need it.


### Linear for product and development work


If your business builds software, there’s usually a mix of new features to work on, bugs to fix, and customer requests to consider.


Linear gives your team a place to organize that work and keep track of what’s moving forward and what’s on the back burner for now.⁵


You can turn a bug report or customer request into a task with an owner and priority, and related tasks can sit together in a project, like launching a new feature. If a bigger goal involves multiple projects, Linear lets you group them into what they call an “initiative.”⁵


That gives you a way to check on a specific task or see how a whole launch is coming along, without asking everyone for a separate update.


## Stay productive and track your time: Toggl Track


You finish a busy week, look at your project list, and wonder where the hours went.


Toggl Track shows you how you spent those hours. You can record time against clients and projects, then review reports to see how long different jobs actually took.⁶ When you’re quoting a similar project, you have those hours to refer back to.


If a job took twice as long as expected, you can use that information to adjust your next quote, allow more time in the schedule, or look at which part of the work kept slowing you down.


## Schedule appointments: Calendly


Finding a time to meet shouldn’t take more back-and-forth than the meeting itself. As such, Calendly lets you share a booking link so clients can choose from your available times.⁷


You can connect your calendar, set your working hours, and add buffers between appointments. Depending on your plan, you can also use reminders, different event types, and team scheduling features.⁷


Use the booking link for consultations, introductory calls, demos, or interviews, and add it to your website or email signature.


If you only need one type of appointment, the free plan includes one event type and unlimited meetings. More complex scheduling needs could require a paid plan.⁸


## Organize your marketing and social media strategy: Canva and Sprout Social


These tools give you a way to create graphics, schedule content ahead of time, and manage customer replies. That way, you’re not starting from scratch every time you need to post or answer a DM.


### Canva for creating visuals across different channels


With Canva, you can turn your marketing offer into an Instagram post, put together an event flyer, or create a presentation using your business’s colors, images, and logo.


You can choose a template, change the text and images, and adjust the layout for what you’re making.⁹


We recommend keeping a few core templates ready in your account. When you have a new offer or announcement, you can swap in fresh images and text without rebuilding your layout.


You can also share those ready-made designs with your team so everyone stays on brand. That keeps your social feed looking polished and saves your colleagues from starting from scratch.


Some advanced templates, stock photos, and AI tools require a paid Canva Pro subscription.⁹


### Sprout Social for managing social media posts and conversations


If you’re managing social accounts for your business, you’re well aware that the work doesn’t stop after publishing a post. There’s always the next post to plan, customer messages to respond to, and finding out what content your audience engages with.


Sprout Social combines post scheduling, a shared social inbox, and reporting analytics into one dashboard. You can prep posts, keep track of messages across supported social platforms, and see how your content performs.¹⁰


You and your teammates can coordinate who’s publishing and who’s responding. If you wind up taking over a customer question, you can read the conversation history before replying.


The available reporting and team features vary by plan, so the number of accounts and people involved will affect the setup you need.¹⁰


## Manage your inventory and shipping: Zoho Inventory


If you sell physical products, you need to know which orders are in stock, which are ready to pack, and what has already shipped.


In Zoho Inventory, you can check stock across locations, track orders, and set reorder levels so you know when it is time to buy more.¹¹


If you sell in a few places, like a physical storefront and an online store, for example, you can also connect those channels to Zoho Inventory so your stock stays updated automatically.¹²


Before choosing a plan, make sure Zoho Inventory connects with your web platform and the courier you use for deliveries in the UAE.


## Run your books and keep accounting in order: Zoho Books


With Zoho Books, you can send invoices, record expenses, and match payments to your transactions as you go. Their UAE edition includes VAT accounting features.¹³


Their mobile app lets you record new expenses as they happen so you have less to track down and organize when tax time comes around. And when you want to check how the business is doing, you can pull up reports to see what’s coming in and where the money is going.


To avoid


[common UAE business tax mistakes](https://ziina.com/blog/uae-corporate-tax-registration) , have your accountant double-check your bookkeeping setup and confirm that your records and tax settings are all in order.


## Manage employees and HR: Deel


Growing your team is exciting, but each new hire brings paperwork: employee documents, onboarding tasks, time-off requests, and payroll.


With Deel, you can manage employee records, pay contractors, and run payroll through one platform.¹⁴


Deel also offers an employer of record service in the UAE.¹⁴ That means Deel can legally employ someone on your behalf and handle their payroll and employment administration.


If your


[business already has a legal entity in the UAE](https://ziina.com/blog/cost-of-setting-up-a-business-in-dubai) , Deel offers payroll services for employees you hire directly.¹⁴


## Share and store files: Google Drive


If you use Google Workspace, you probably spend plenty of time in Gmail keeping up with clients and Google Calendar organizing your week.


We do, too, and Google Drive is one of the most important parts of that daily routine. It earns a spot on our list because it makes sharing files and working on them together so straightforward.


Google Drive lets you store files in shared folders and give people permission to view, comment, or edit. Your team can open the same document through a link, with access from a browser, computer, or phone.¹⁵


For a client project, you could keep the brief, assets, working documents, and final files in one folder. Sharing the folder gives everyone a single source of truth to work from.


For us, having one shared place to work gives our team instant answers to the age-old question: “Where’s the latest version?”


## Use AI assistance: Claude


Claude is our AI tool of choice for brainstorming and making sense of the notes and feedback that build up while you’re running a business.


You could give it customer feedback and ask it to group recurring requests, pull outstanding questions from meeting notes, or explore ideas for a new service.¹⁶


You can also use Claude Cowork for workflow automation, such as scheduled tasks. For instance, you could organize recorded sync calls in Notion every Monday, so you have a regular place to find and revisit those conversations.¹⁷


## Design your website and products: Figma


When you describe your vision for a product page in a team chat, everyone will probably picture something different.


With Figma, you and your designer can work directly from the same canvas. You get to review page layouts, click through interactive prototypes, and leave comments on the exact element you want to give feedback on.¹⁸


We like that this lets our team weigh in on new page structures and mobile app updates before developers start writing code.


Figma is less of a daily business app and more of a design platform best used on a computer. As a founder, you can use shared access to review progress and approve visual concepts with your team.


## Track customer engagement and relationships: Braze


Sending the same message to every customer isn’t always the best move.


With Braze, you can welcome new customers, guide them through getting started, or reconnect with people who haven’t used your service in a while. You can coordinate those messages across email, push notifications, and in-app messaging, using customer information and activity to decide who receives what and when.¹⁹


For example, you could set up reminders to go out to customers who signed up but haven’t completed an important next step, and then stop that reminder once they have.


## Final thoughts from the Ziina team


We know how much work goes into running a business beyond the products or services you sell. We’re coordinating projects, planning content, and keeping up with customers, too.


That’s the perspective we brought to this list, and we hope you’ve found a few ideas for your own workday.


It’s also what shapes the way we build Ziina. Getting paid should fit into how you already do business, whether you’re taking orders through social media, selling online, or meeting customers in person.
